title: Synthetic schedule and evidence playbook for SLO drift
author: Emily Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the synthetic-testing schedule, evidence collection, runbook steps, and communications templates to detect, triage, and resolve SLO drift for latency and error-rate SLOs in LLM inference services. It is intended for oncall operators, SREs, and incident owners who manage gradual or subtle SLO regressions ("drift") that are not immediately obvious from traffic spikes.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood's hosted and dedicated inference endpoints (text generation, chat, embeddings).
- Focuses on sustained regressions: 15m–24h windows where p50/p95 latency or token error rate exceed configured thresholds.

Owner & roles:
- Incident owner: service owner oncall (primary).
- Evidence custodian: SRE oncall (collects traces/logs/synthetics).
- Bridge conductor: oncall Lead or incident commander if incident escalates.
- Customer communications: Customer Success (CS) + Incident Owner.

Definitions & thresholds:
- SLO drift alert: 15m p95 latency > target * 1.25 OR token error-rate increase > +0.5 percentage points vs baseline.
- Baseline: rolling 7d median of the metric at the same hour-of-day.

Detection & synthetic schedule (recommended):
Run synthetic probes targeted at representative routes and model sizes. Schedule below is minimum — increase cadence for high-risk releases.

| Probe | Target | Frequency | Owner | Success criteria |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Quick-chat (short inputs) | chat-route-prod | 1m | Synthetics team | p95 < 200ms + no partial-token errors |
| Long-context generation (2k tokens) | gen-long-prod | 5m | Synthetics team | median < 800ms + token-error-rate < 0.5% |
| Embedding consistency | embed-prod | 15m | Synthetics team | vector-norm deviation < 0.01 vs baseline |

Evidence collection checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Mark alert and assign incident owner.
2) Snapshot: capture 15m and 1h windows for affected metrics (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, queue-length).
3) Pull traces for 95th percentile requests and representative successful/failed traces.
4) Collect synthetic probe results and full payloads for last 2h.
5) Record rollout metadata: model version(s), routing policy, recent canaries, autoscaling events, new infra patches.
6) Note correlated signals: infra CPU/GPU utilization, network egress errors, backing-store latencies (KV, DB), throttling events.

Immediate runbook (triage & containment):
1. Confirm: verify the synthetic probe failures are reproducible and not a transient metric blip.
2. Scope: determine customer-impact (tenant-aware) and service domains affected.
3. Contain: if p95 latency breaches SLO and impacts customers, apply fallback routing to a compatible model-variant or regional pool. Steps:
   - CLI: redwood route set --service <svc> --policy fallback --variant <compatible-model>
   - Apply for affected route(s) only; monitor synthetic success within 2m.
4. Throttle/backpressure: if queueing is causing tail latency, reduce per-route concurrency limits or enable autoscale-burst for Dedicated tenants.
5. Mitigate: consider temporary quantization rollback or revert of recent kernel selection changes; coordinate with runtime team.

Escalation matrix & timing:
- 0–15m: service oncall (detect & evidence).
- 15–45m: SRE bridge + runtime engineer if infra signals present.
- 45–90m: Eng lead + Product + CS for customer notices; consider SLA credit assessment.
- >90m: Exec pager and account-level brief for enterprise customers.

Game day (synthetic drift exercise) plan (quarterly):
- Objective: validate detection, evidence collection, fallbacks, and customer comms for slow SLO drift scenarios.
- Participants: oncall SREs, runtime, CS, product, oncall lead.
- Duration: 3 hours per exercise + 1h retro.
- Script sample:
  1) Week 0: create scheduled synthetic that increases median latency by +30% over baseline for 90m via fault-injection on staging.
  2) Trigger oncall alerting and require evidence checklist completion within 20m.
  3) Require a safe fallback (routing to variant) executed within 40m.

Post-incident evidence & postmortem template (required fields):
- Timeline (UTC timestamps)  — detection, escalation, mitigation steps, closure.
- Key metrics (charts embedded): 7d baseline vs incident windows.
- Synthetic probe logs and payloads (attach files).
- Traces: representative 95th percentile trace + text snippets of error messages.
- Root cause hypothesis and supporting evidence.
- Action items (owner, ETA, verification steps).

Customer status template (short form for incidents under review):
Subject: Incident update — inference latency impacting some requests
Body:
Hello [CustomerName],
We are investigating higher-than-normal latency for inference requests to [service/region]. Our engineers have applied temporary routing to reduce impact while we continue diagnosis. We will provide the next update in 60 minutes.
Sincerely,
Redwood Incident Team

Verification & closure criteria:
- Synthetic probes show recovery for two consecutive monitoring windows matching pre-incident baseline (5m and 15m aggregated).
- Postmortem created and reviewed within 5 business days.
- All action items have owners and verification steps.

Rotation integration & responsibilities:
- Oncall owners must validate synthetic probes at start-of-shift (check green for primary probes).
- SREs own evidence custody for the incident.
- Runtime engineers own fallback rollbacks and kernel selection rollouts.

Appendix: sample synthetic config (YAML)
---
probe_name: quick-chat-prod
target: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
input_snippet: "Hello"
expected_status: 200
max_p95_latency_ms: 200
frequency_seconds: 60
alerting: |
  severity: warning
  condition: p95 > 200ms for 3 windows
---

Appendix: quick verification commands
- Pull p95 latency: rwh metrics query --service inference --metric p95_latency --window 15m
- Get recent routing policy: rwh route get --service <svc>
- Apply temporary fallback: rwh route set --service <svc> --policy fallback --variant <model-v1-compat>

Frequently asked questions:
Q: When should we provide customers a formal status page entry?
A: If >3 customers are affected or any enterprise tenant reports impact, publish a public status page entry within 90 minutes.

Q: Who signs off postmortem?
A: Incident owner + SRE lead + affected service tech lead.
